Domain knowledge for short-read quality control, trimming, and

## Expected Workflow

   - read length
   - expected adapters or library type

description: Domain knowledge for short-read alignment and post-alignment processing.

# Sequence Alignment

Domain knowledge for aligning short reads to a reference genome and
processing the resulting alignments.

## Expected Workflow

1. Check the dataset and assay facts first:
   - read layout
   - assay type
   - reference genome and index
   - whether downstream steps depend on pairing semantics
2. Choose an aligner and mode that match the assay instead of reusing a
   familiar default blindly.
3. Treat mapping rate and summary statistics as a sanity check on the
   reference and alignment mode.
4. Apply post-alignment filters deliberately and document what each one
   removes.
5. Accept the alignment branch only if sort order, indexing, and summary
   files all match the delivered BAM.

## Alignment Basics

item_id: wf_006_atacseq_chromatin_accessibility
query: 'Identify open-chromatin regions in the provided paired-end human ATAC-seq
  sample using the hg19 assembly.

  Remove Nextera adapters by mate-overlap analysis. Treat bases below Phred 20 as
  low quality, and discard a pair if either mate contains more than 70 percent low-quality
  bases or is shorter than 15 bases after adapter trimming.

  Align the surviving pairs to hg19 with a suitable paired-end short-read aligner.
  Retain pairs that the selected aligner classifies as valid paired-end alignments,
  with mapping quality at least 30, remove mitochondrial alignments, and remove PCR
  duplicates.

  Call open-chromatin regions on the resulting alignments with a peak caller suitable
  for ATAC-seq, using a q-value cutoff of 0.05 and no control sample.

  Write the results to `final_answer/peaks.bed`, with chromosome, start, and end in
  the first three tab-separated columns. Report one BED record for every interval
  your peak
